learn.hook: Rub a leaf, sniff a flower, touch the bark. Plants are full of surprises!
points: Trees are tall plants with one thick, hard, woody stem called a trunk, like neem, mango and banyan.
Shrubs are medium-sized plants with many hard stems close to the ground, like rose and hibiscus (gudhal).
Herbs are small plants with soft green stems, like coriander (dhania), mint (pudina) and wheat.
Climbers have weak stems and climb up with support, like the money plant and the pea plant. Creepers spread on the ground, like pumpkin and watermelon.
We can observe leaves, bark, flowers and fruits by looking, touching gently and smelling, without plucking them.

example.q: Think it through: A plant in Asha's garden is small, with a soft green stem. Its leaves smell fresh and are used in chutney. What kind of plant is it?
steps: It is small with a soft green stem.
Small plants with soft green stems are herbs.
Mint and coriander are herbs used in chutney.
example.answer: It is a herb, like mint or coriander.

learn.reallife: On a nature walk, place a paper on a leaf and rub it gently with a crayon. The leaf's veins will appear like magic!

games.title: Plant facts
items: A tree has a thick, hard, woody trunk.
The trunk holds up the tall tree.
A pumpkin plant is a creeper.
Its stem is weak, so it spreads along the ground.
Herbs are small plants with soft green stems.
The leaves of the touch-me-not plant fold up when touched.
This plant is also called chhui-mui. Its leaves close when you touch them.
We should pluck many flowers to observe them well.
We can observe flowers on the plant without plucking them.

quiz.q: Which of these is a tree?
quiz.explain: A mango plant grows tall with a thick woody trunk, so it is a tree.
steps: Trees are tall plants with a thick, woody trunk.
Mango grows into a tall tree; mint is a herb, rose a shrub, pea a climber.
Answer: Mango
quiz.mistake: Thinks any plant with fruits or flowers is a tree

quiz.q: A money plant grows up a wall with the help of a stick. What kind of plant is it?
quiz.explain: A money plant has a weak stem and climbs up with support, so it is a climber.
steps: Climbers have weak stems and climb up with support.
The money plant climbs a wall with a stick.
Answer: Climber
quiz.mistake: Mixes up climbers and creepers

quiz.q: Which part of a tree is the thick, hard stem?
quiz.explain: The thick, hard stem of a tree is called the trunk.
steps: The thick, hard stem of a tree is called the trunk.
Answer: Trunk
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name of a tree's main stem

quiz.q: A plant is medium-sized and has many hard stems near the ground. It grows red flowers. What is it?
quiz.explain: Medium plants with many hard stems close to the ground are shrubs, like the hibiscus.
steps: Medium-sized plants with many hard stems near the ground are shrubs.
Hibiscus is an example.
Answer: A shrub
quiz.mistake: Mixes up shrubs with trees or herbs

quiz.q: Which plant spreads along the ground because its stem is weak?
quiz.explain: A watermelon plant is a creeper. Its weak stem spreads along the ground.
steps: Creepers have weak stems and spread on the ground.
Watermelon is a creeper; neem, banyan and peepal are trees.
Answer: Watermelon
quiz.mistake: Thinks a big fruit must grow on a tree

quiz.q: The banyan tree has roots that hang down from its branches into the soil. What do these roots do?
options: They help hold up the big branches
quiz.explain: These hanging roots grow into the soil and act like pillars that support the wide branches.
steps: The banyan's roots hang from branches into the soil.
They act like pillars for the wide branches.
Answer: They help hold up the big branches
quiz.mistake: Does not know that roots can grow above the ground

quiz.q: What is the best way to observe a flower on a nature trail?
options: Look closely, smell it gently and leave it on the plant
quiz.explain: We can learn a lot just by looking and smelling. Leaving the flower lets bees visit it too.
steps: We observe plants by looking, touching gently and smelling, without plucking.
Answer: Look closely, smell it gently and leave it on the plant
quiz.mistake: Thinks we must pick a plant to study it

quiz.q: Which of these is a herb?
quiz.explain: Coriander is a small plant with a soft green stem, so it is a herb.
steps: Herbs are small plants with soft green stems.
Coriander is a herb; hibiscus is a shrub; banyan and neem are trees.
Answer: Coriander
quiz.mistake: Does not know the features of a herb

teach.ask: Gappu sees big plants and small plants. How can we tell a tree, a shrub and a herb apart?
teach.praise: Fantastic! Trees have thick trunks, shrubs have many hard stems and herbs have soft green stems.
teach.nudge: Look at the stem! What is the stem like on a tree, a shrub and a herb?

revise.summary: Plants can be trees, shrubs, herbs, climbers or creepers, depending on their size and stem. We observe plants by looking, touching gently and smelling, without plucking.
focus: Telling trees, shrubs, herbs, climbers and creepers apart
Parts like the trunk and banyan's hanging roots
remember: Tree: tall, one thick woody trunk (neem, mango, banyan)
Shrub: medium, many hard stems near the ground (rose, hibiscus)
Herb: small, soft green stem (coriander, mint, wheat)
Climber climbs with support (money plant, pea); creeper spreads on ground (pumpkin, watermelon)
traps: Don't call a money plant a creeper; it climbs, so it is a climber.
Don't pluck flowers to observe them.

learn.hook: Shh! Sit still and listen. Can you hear a bird, a bee or a cricket?
points: Insects have 6 legs and 3 main body parts. Ants, bees and butterflies are insects.
Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.
Birds have feathers and beaks. The shape of a beak suits the food a bird eats.
A butterfly grows in four stages: egg, caterpillar, pupa and adult butterfly.
We observe animals quietly from a distance. We never disturb nests, eggs or baby animals.

example.q: Think it through: A kingfisher has a long, pointed beak. What food is it best for?
steps: A long, pointed beak is like a spear.
It can grab slippery things quickly.
Kingfishers dive into water to catch fish.

learn.reallife: Keep a nature diary. Each morning, write down the birds you see or hear near your home.

games.title: Match the beak to its food
pairs: Digs insects out of tree bark

quiz.q: How many legs does an insect have?
quiz.explain: All insects, like ants, bees and butterflies, have 6 legs.
steps: Insects have 6 legs and 3 main body parts.
Answer: 6
quiz.mistake: Mixes up insects with spiders

quiz.q: Why is a spider not an insect?
quiz.explain: Insects have 6 legs. Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.
steps: Insects have 6 legs.
Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.
Answer: It has 8 legs
quiz.mistake: Thinks every small creepy-crawly is an insect

quiz.q: A spider has 8 legs and an ant has 6 legs. How many more legs does the spider have?
quiz.explain: 8 − 6 = 2. A spider has 2 more legs than an ant.
steps: Spider legs: 8
Ant legs: 6
Answer: 2
quiz.mistake: Adds the legs instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: What comes out of a butterfly's egg?
quiz.explain: A caterpillar hatches from the egg. Later it becomes a pupa and then a butterfly.
steps: Butterfly stages: egg → caterpillar → pupa → adult.
So a caterpillar comes out of the egg.
Answer: A caterpillar
quiz.mistake: Thinks a butterfly comes straight out of the egg

quiz.q: Which body covering do all birds have?
quiz.explain: Feathers are found only on birds. They keep birds warm and help most of them fly.
steps: Birds have feathers and beaks.
Fur, spines and shells belong to other animals.
Answer: Feathers
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the body coverings of birds and other animals

quiz.q: A sunbird has a long, thin beak. What does it mostly feed on?
quiz.explain: A long, thin beak can reach deep inside flowers to sip sweet nectar.
steps: A beak's shape suits the bird's food.
A long, thin beak reaches deep inside flowers for nectar.
Answer: Nectar from flowers
quiz.mistake: Does not link the shape of a beak with the food a bird eats

quiz.q: You spot a bird's nest with eggs in a bush. What should you do?
options: Poke the nest with a stick
quiz.explain: Watching from far away keeps the eggs and the parent birds safe.
steps: We never disturb nests or eggs.
We watch quietly from a distance.
Answer: Watch quietly from a distance
quiz.mistake: Does not know that disturbing nests harms birds

quiz.q: Which stage of a butterfly's life comes just before the adult butterfly?
quiz.explain: The order is egg, caterpillar, pupa, butterfly. The pupa comes just before the butterfly.
steps: Order: egg, caterpillar, pupa, butterfly.
The pupa comes just before the adult.
Answer: Pupa
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of the life cycle

teach.ask: Gappu found a six-legged ant and an eight-legged spider. Are they both insects? And how should we watch animals?
teach.praise: Great observing! Insects have six legs, spiders have eight, and we watch animals quietly from far away.
teach.nudge: Count the legs! How many legs does an insect have?

revise.summary: Insects have 6 legs and 3 main body parts; spiders have 8 legs and are not insects. Birds have feathers and beaks shaped for their food. A butterfly grows from egg to caterpillar to pupa to adult.
remember: Insects: 6 legs, 3 body parts (ants, bees, butterflies)
Long thin beak: nectar; long pointed beak (kingfisher): fish
traps: A spider is not an insect.
A caterpillar, not a butterfly, comes out of the egg.

topics.title: Biodiversity: so many kinds of life

learn.hook: From tiny ants to giant elephants, India is home to an amazing variety of life!
points: Biodiversity means the great variety of plants and animals found in a place.
Different animals and plants live in different places: forests, deserts, rivers, seas and mountains.
Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros. Gir in Gujarat is the home of Asiatic lions.
The Sundarbans in West Bengal have mangrove forests and the Royal Bengal tiger. Snow leopards live high in the Himalayas.
The tiger is India's national animal, the peacock is our national bird and the lotus is our national flower.

example.q: Think it through: A forest has many kinds of trees, birds, insects and animals. Why is this good?
steps: Each living thing has a job in nature.
Bees help flowers, birds spread seeds, and trees give shelter.
If many kinds live together, nature stays balanced and healthy.
example.answer: A forest with high biodiversity stays healthy because living things help each other.

learn.reallife: Count how many different kinds of birds, insects and plants you can see in a park. That is the biodiversity of your park!

games.title: Match the place to its famous animal

quiz.q: What does biodiversity mean?
options: The variety of plants and animals in a place
Only one kind of plant in a place
The number of houses in a town
quiz.explain: Bio means life and diversity means variety. Biodiversity is the variety of living things.
steps: Bio = life, diversity = variety.
Biodiversity is the variety of plants and animals in a place.
Answer: The variety of plants and animals in a place
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the word biodiversity

quiz.q: Which national park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros?
quiz.explain: Kaziranga in Assam is home to most of the world's one-horned rhinoceroses.
steps: Kaziranga National Park is in Assam.
It is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.
Answer: Kaziranga
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the famous national parks of India

quiz.q: Where in India do Asiatic lions live in the wild?
quiz.explain: Gir and the forests around it in Gujarat are the only wild home of Asiatic lions.
steps: Asiatic lions live in Gir, Gujarat.
Answer: Gir in Gujarat
quiz.mistake: Mixes up lions and tigers or their homes

quiz.q: Which is the national bird of India?
quiz.explain: The peacock (Indian peafowl) is India's national bird.
steps: India's national bird is the peacock.
Answer: Peacock
quiz.mistake: Picks a common bird instead of the national bird

quiz.q: The Sundarbans have special trees that grow in salty, muddy water near the sea. What are these forests called?
quiz.explain: Mangroves grow where rivers meet the sea. The Sundarbans have one of the largest mangrove forests.
steps: Trees that grow in salty, muddy water near the sea are mangroves.
The Sundarbans have mangrove forests.
Answer: Mangrove forests
quiz.mistake: Does not know the kind of forest in the Sundarbans

quiz.q: Which animal lives high in the cold, snowy Himalayas?
quiz.explain: The snow leopard has thick fur and lives in the cold Himalayan mountains.
steps: Snow leopards live high in the Himalayas.
Their thick fur keeps them warm.
Answer: Snow leopard
quiz.mistake: Does not link animals with where they live

quiz.q: Which is the national flower of India?
quiz.explain: The lotus is India's national flower.
steps: India's national flower is the lotus.
Answer: Lotus
quiz.mistake: Picks a popular flower instead of the national flower

quiz.q: Why is it important to protect the many kinds of plants and animals?
options: Because animals are only for zoos
Because living things depend on each other to keep nature balanced
quiz.explain: When one kind of living thing disappears, others that depend on it are harmed too.
steps: Living things depend on each other.
When one kind disappears, others are harmed.
Answer: Because living things depend on each other to keep nature balanced
quiz.mistake: Thinks losing one kind of living thing does not matter

teach.ask: Gappu heard the big word biodiversity. What does it mean, and why should we care?
teach.praise: Awesome! Biodiversity is the variety of plants and animals, and we must protect it to keep nature balanced.
teach.nudge: Does biodiversity mean one kind of animal, or many kinds of living things?

revise.summary: Biodiversity is the variety of plants and animals in a place. Different living things live in forests, deserts, rivers, seas and mountains, and India has special parks and national symbols.
remember: Kaziranga (Assam): one-horned rhinoceros; Gir (Gujarat): Asiatic lions
Sundarbans (West Bengal): mangroves and Royal Bengal tiger
Snow leopards live high in the Himalayas
National animal: tiger; bird: peacock; flower: lotus
traps: Asiatic lions live in Gir, not Kaziranga.
Every kind of living thing matters, not only big animals.
